raw_response:
I will still lean on wheat and maize, because that is what feeds the house and brings the steadier money here. Last year’s way is my starting point, and I will not turn too much just to try something fancy. Out of my 8 mu, I will keep 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that land and my well water fit it best. I will leave 1 mu for cotton and 1 mu for mungbean, just so I have some cash crop and some short-season crop without pressing too hard on the budget. When I am unsure, I do what I saw work on nearby fields: wheat cannot be starved, maize needs a full mouth if I want ears to fill, cotton needs more spraying than grain crops, and mungbean I keep light because if I spend too much on it, the money does not always come back. I count every bag, but I would still put a little extra fertilizer on wheat and maize rather than watch the yield fall.
